items.title: Henry "Pickle" Jackson Interview, 1961-08-09
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...how did it compare, say, with Count Basie or Lunsford or some of those other big bands? ... [INTERVIEWEE] At the time, I think the band compared as powerful as Count Basie's band...

ctx.x: That's right, the whole band. Numbers like High Society, we had a number they called Backbeat Booger. We had another number they called Red. We had a lot of Booger Woogers that just played when somebody asked for it. They said, play me Booger Wooger. And the music was forgotten about that. And everybody could play. The whole band could get together on that too. The whole band could get together. We all could get together, swing that. And there'd be many times that X's would put the music up. And X's would close…

I never did get to hear it. I might have heard the band once. Oh, 1942 or something. When I first was around here. But how did it compare? I mean, it might be difficult for you to judge yourself if you were playing in it. But how did it compare, say, with Count Basie or Lunsford or some of those other big bands? Did it seem as powerful and as big as... Well, at the time...

How did it compare, do you think? At the time, I think the band compared as powerful as Count Basie's band at the time because they had a lot of young musicians in it and a lot of good ones. And they could play. They could blow. And to me, the musician was just as good as any musician you could find anywhere in the world. Just as good as musicians you could find in Count Basie. Maybe Basie might have been playing a different type of music. Or might have been playing a little fast or something like that. But as…
